input.quote: At the request of Harpoon, AbbVie shall permit an independent public accounting firm of nationally recognized standing designated by Harpoon and reasonably acceptable to AbbVie, [***], to audit the books and records maintained pursuant to this Section 6.11
input.rationale: Section 6.11 is the audit right exercisable against us. The auditor is independent and of nationally recognized standing and reasonably acceptable to AbbVie, and disclosure to Harpoon is limited to correctness and discrepancies. But the audit is triggered simply \"at the request of Harpoon\" with no advance notice and no business-hours or off-site limitation, the accounting firm itself is not bound by confidentiality (Section 6.13 binds only the Audit Expert), there is no bar on direct access to our systems, and both the frequency cap and the cost-shifting variance threshold are redacted so neither the 12-month cap nor a 5% threshold can be verified. That fails the fallback on material terms. Our redline fixes the frequency to once in any 12-month period and cost-shifting to a variance exceeding 5%, and adds 30 days' prior written notice, normal business hours, off-site conduct where possible, no direct system access, and confidentiality obligations on the auditing firm.

ops.oldText: (b) be conducted more than once in any [***] period
ops.newText: (b) be conducted more than once in any 12-month period

ops.oldText: a variance [***] from the reported amounts
ops.newText: a variance exceeding 5% from the reported amounts

ops.text: Any such audit shall be conducted on 30 days' prior written notice, during AbbVie's normal business hours and off-site where possible, without direct access to AbbVie's systems, and the accounting firm shall be bound by written confidentiality obligations.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We fixed the redacted audit limits to no more than once in any 12-month period and cost-shifting only on a variance exceeding 5%, and added 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, off-site conduct, no direct system access and confidentiality for the auditing firm.
proposal.summary: Cap Section 6.11 audits at once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, during business hours, off-site, with no system access, a confidentiality-bound auditor and cost-shifting only above a 5% variance

mappings.element: No more than one audit per 12 months.
